fix(composed-modal): make closed modal inert

Fixes #2338

Closed modals were capturing interactions during the 240ms fade-out
transition. The CSS delays `visibility: hidden` by 240ms, leaving
the modal interactive while invisible. Added `inert` attribute when
`open={false}` to disable all interactions (mouse, keyboard, focus)
and remove from accessibility tree during transition.

Fixes #1537

When tabs were conditionally rendered using Svelte's {#if} blocks,
their indices would desync from DOM order. Removed tabs were never
cleaned up from internal stores, causing re-added tabs to receive
incorrect indices (e.g., Tab 1 toggled off/on would change from
index 0 to 3).

type — the walker only sees DOM-string ids, which wouldn't match numeric
ids in the store. Skip disabled nodes and any row whose element carries
`bx--tree-node--hidden`. Also drop the now-redundant aria-disabled /

already excludes those rows.

`afterUpdate` guarded by node identity, so dynamic node updates (filter,
swap, reload) keep a focusable entry point. Selector also skips
`bx--tree-node--hidden`, and the link variant (`<a role="treeitem">`)
is now eligible.

fix(tree-view-item): ArrowRight reliably focuses the first child row

`firstTreeItemInGroup` helper so the first child row is found even when
it's a link node — `<li role="none"> > <a role="treeitem">` — not just
a bare `<li>`. Also drop the local `expanded = true` mutation in favor
of letting the expanded store drive the reactive value.

fix(tree-view-item): Enter toggles expand on parent; Space only selects

Match the ARIA tree pattern (and Carbon React): Space selects the parent
row without toggling its expansion; only Enter toggles. Both the
keyboard handler and the toggle button click now drive `expanded`
exclusively through the expanded store rather than via a local
mutation.

fix(tree-view-item): wire aria-owns and aria-labelledby for subtree group

reference it from the parent row via `aria-owns`, and label it with the
parent's text via `aria-labelledby` pointing at a new wrapper span
(`<parentId>__label`). Adjust the brittle DOM-walk in the existing
"can expand some nodes" test to a role-based query, since the new label
wrapper shifts the depth one level deeper.

fix(slider): clamp keyboard value and dispatch `change` from commit gestures

The keydown handler set `value = Math.round((value + delta) / step) * step`
without clamping, so an ArrowRight at `max` dispatched `input` with an
out-of-range payload (e.g. 101 for max 100). The reactive block repaired
the bound `value` before paint, but the `input` event had already fired
with the unclamped number. Clamp inline before dispatching.

`change` was already emitted, but from the global reactive block, which
ran on any `value` change including programmatic/consumer updates. Move
it into the commit gestures (keydown, drag end, text-input change) so it
only fires on a real user commit, and drop it from the reactive block.

Add unit coverage for the keyboard clamp and that `change` no longer
fires on programmatic value updates, plus an e2e max-boundary check.

does not fit. Because the flip is decided from the floating element's
width, a tooltip whose text swaps to something narrower (e.g. CopyButton
showing "Copied!" after a wide hover description) would un-flip back to
the preferred side mid-session, making it jump sides — or render clipped.

Add `lockDirection` to FloatingPortal (opt-in, default off so menus are
unaffected) and `lockedDirection` to floatingPosition. Once the content
flips away from the preferred direction, that side is latched for the
open session and reused on later updates, so a content resize no longer
re-triggers a flip. The latch fires only after a real flip, so the
initial layout passes (which run before a side-placed tooltip's final
width is known) can still settle on the correct side. PortalTooltip opts
in, fixing the side jump on CopyButton/CopyInput tooltips.

fix(utils): defer dismiss() window listener registration past the enabling click

A control outside a menu/tooltip/popover's anchor that sets its bound
`open` to true from a click handler would immediately close what it
just opened: enabling `use:dismiss` registers its window click
listener synchronously, and in this environment the SAME click
event's bubble phase can still reach `window` after that
registration — heavy synchronous DOM work in the opening handler
(mounting a portal, positioning it) delays the event's arrival past a
microtask flush, so even a `queueMicrotask` defer isn't enough. Defer
registration to the next task with `setTimeout` instead, which
reliably waits out the current dispatch.

fix(floating-portal)!: change `lockDirection` to enum

FloatingPortal recomputed the top/bottom (or left/right) flip on
every scroll- and resize-driven reposition, so a floating element
could flip sides mid-interaction as the anchor's on-screen position
changed.

Adds a `lockDirection` prop: `"none" | "after-flip" | "always"`.
- "after-flip": recompute freely until the content first flips away
  from the preferred side, then hold that side for the rest of the
  open session, so a later content resize (e.g. a tooltip whose text
  changes to something narrower) doesn't snap it back. PortalTooltip
  opts into this.
- "always": lock whichever side the initial open settles on, flipped
  or not, once the open-time layout passes finish, so later
  scroll/resize/mutation updates only reposition along that side
  instead of re-running the flip check.

fix(structured-list): stop mixing table and radio/checkbox ARIA roles (#3420)

Selectable StructuredList rows render as <label role="radio"> (or
role="checkbox" when multiple), overriding the row's role to convey
selection state. But the wrapper still unconditionally applied
role="table", and StructuredListHead/StructuredListBody/
StructuredListCell unconditionally applied role="rowgroup" and
role="cell"/"columnheader". A table/rowgroup ancestor chain requires
row children, and cell/columnheader requires a row ancestor -- axe-core
flags both directions of the broken relationship (aria-required-children,
aria-required-parent), plus radio not being an allowed role on <label>
at all (aria-allowed-role).

Fix: gate the table/rowgroup/row/cell/columnheader roles off entirely
when selection is active, and give StructuredListBody a radiogroup
(single-select) or group (multi-select) role instead, matching vanilla
Carbon's own selectable structured-list markup, which never used table
roles for this variant either.

Also give the selection-icon header cell (rendered automatically by
StructuredListRow when selection is on) a visually-hidden label -- it
previously rendered with no text at all, which axe separately flags as
an empty table header.

fix(multi-select): stop option checkboxes from being independently focusable (#3421)

MultiSelect renders each option as a role="option" div using a
roving-tabindex pattern, with tabindex="-1" passed to the inner
Checkbox so the visual checkbox itself never enters the tab order.
That tabindex never reached the actual <input>: Checkbox.svelte's
$$restProps is documented and spread onto the wrapper <div>, not the
input, so the attribute landed on an inert element. The checkbox kept
its native default tabbable state, leaving every option with a
focusable descendant -- axe-core's nested-interactive check flags
this as a WCAG 4.1.2 violation, and it lets keyboard/screen-reader
users tab directly into a checkbox nested inside an already-focusable
listbox option.

Add an explicit tabindex prop to Checkbox that applies to the <input>
directly. This is additive and defaults to undefined, so every other
Checkbox consumer is unaffected; MultiSelect's existing tabindex="-1"
usage now binds to the new prop instead of falling through to
$$restProps, fixing both the virtualized and non-virtualized render
paths with no MultiSelect.svelte changes required.

fix(data-table): label row checkboxes and fix expand column headers (#3424)

Three related accessibility gaps in DataTable:

- Per-row batch-selection checkboxes had no accessible name (the
  select-all header checkbox was labelled "Select all rows", but the
  row-level InlineCheckbox instances passed no aria-label at all).
- The expand column's <td headers="expand"> referenced a <th> id that
  was never actually set, so the reference was always dangling.
- The expand column's <th> rendered with no text content at all when
  batchExpansion was off, since only the batchExpansion branch had any
  content.

Label each row checkbox, scope the expand column's id to the table
instance's internal id (so multiple DataTables on one page don't
collide on a literal "expand" id) and reference it from both the
normal and virtual-scroll row render paths, and always render
(visually-hidden when unbatched) text in the expand header.

fix(tabs): remove tabindex from the presentational <li> wrapper (#3422)

The <li role="presentation"> wrapping each <a role="tab"> also
carried tabindex="-1". Per HTML-AAM role-conflict resolution, a
presentational element that is focusable is not flattened out of the
accessibility tree, so browsers kept the <li> as a list item between
the tablist and its tabs, breaking the required direct
tablist -> tab relationship that axe-core checks for.

fix(tooltip): default `iconDescription` is "Show information" (#3423)

Tooltip's iconDescription prop defaulted to "", so mounting <Tooltip>
without explicitly setting iconDescription or triggerText -- the
component's most minimal usage -- rendered an icon-only trigger with
aria-label="" and no other accessible name. The empty string is worse
than an absent attribute, since it suppresses any other name
computation the browser might otherwise fall back to.

Every other icon-only trigger in this codebase (OverflowMenu,
CopyButton) defaults its description prop to a real string; Tooltip
was the outlier. Default iconDescription to a non-empty string to
match that convention, so the default tooltip trigger has an
accessible name out of the box.

fix(date-picker): mark out-of-range calendar days as aria-disabled (#3425)

Previous/next-month and out-of-range calendar days render with
Carbon's own text-disabled color, inherited unchanged from
carbon-components' _date-picker.scss. That pairing fails WCAG 1.4.3
contrast against the calendar background, but the days carried only
a flatpickr-disabled CSS class with no ARIA signal, so axe-core's
color-contrast check had no way to recognize them as an inactive UI
component and exempt them.

Mark these days aria-disabled="true" via flatpickr's onDayCreate
hook, composed as an array so any consumer-supplied
flatpickrProps.onDayCreate keeps running alongside it.

fix(ui-shell): stop `HeaderSearch` referencing non-existent menu id (#3426)

HeaderSearch set aria-owns and aria-controls to a fixed `${id}-menu`
id unconditionally, but the element carrying that id only renders
once the field is active (open). aria-activedescendant had the same
problem: selectedId is derived from the results/selectedResultIndex
props alone, with no dependency on active, so it resolved to a
menuitem id that doesn't exist in the DOM until the field opens.
Any consumer that populates `results` up front -- the normal way to
use this prop -- ships a closed search field with three dangling ARIA
references, which axe-core flags as aria-valid-attr-value violations.

Gate aria-owns, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant on `active`
so they're only set once the referenced element actually exists.

fix(selectable-tile): `SelectableTile` does not use incorrect `role="checkbox"` (#3427)

SelectableTile put role="checkbox" and aria-checked directly on the
<label> wrapping each tile, with the actual <input type="checkbox">
removed from the tab order (tabindex="-1"). role="checkbox" isn't an
ARIA-in-HTML-allowed role for <label> elements, which axe-core flags
as aria-allowed-role.

Fixed by mirroring RadioTile's pattern: the native <input> is now the
focusable, checkbox-shaped element (tabindex driven by the component's
own tabindex prop, change/keydown handlers moved onto it), and the
<label> goes back to being a plain native label with no role,
aria-checked, or tabindex of its own. This preserves the existing
click hit area (the label still wraps the tile content and forwards
clicks to the input) while keeping Tab focus and Enter/Space toggling
working exactly as before.

fix(composed-modal): fall back to title for the dialog's accessible name (#3428)

ComposedModal's role="dialog" got its aria-label exclusively from
ModalHeader's `label` prop -- a secondary eyebrow string shown above
the heading, not the heading itself. `title` (the actual modal
heading, rendered as an <h3> with no id) never fed the accessible
name at all. Since `label` defaults to "" and the derivation used
`??`, a modal with only `title` set -- the common case -- got
aria-label="" instead of falling through: nullish coalescing doesn't
treat an empty string as absent.

Track `title` through the same "carbon:ComposedModal" context
mechanism `label` already uses, and fall back to it (using `||`, so
empty strings are correctly treated as unset) in the aria-label
derivation. Matches how the simpler Modal component already falls
back to modalHeading.

fix(structured-list): move radio/checkbox role off selectable row (#3431)

StructuredListRow put role="radio"/"checkbox" and aria-checked
directly on the <label> wrapping each selectable row, with the
associated <input> hardcoded to tabindex="-1" and aria-hidden.
role="radio"/"checkbox" isn't an ARIA-in-HTML-allowed role for
<label> elements, which axe-core flags as aria-allowed-role. This is
independent of the table/rowgroup gating landed in 881d19dbe.

Mirror SelectableTile's fix (e5a9c2c9e): StructuredListInput's native
<input> becomes the real focusable, checkbox/radio-shaped element
(own tabindex prop, Enter-to-toggle keydown handler, no more
aria-hidden/tabindex="-1"), and StructuredListRow's <label> goes back
to a plain wrapper with no role/aria-checked/tabindex of its own.

Carbon's base CSS sets `.bx--structured-list-input { display: none }`,
which would leave the newly-focusable input untabbable and hidden
from assistive tech in real browsers even though it passes in jsdom
(no stylesheet loaded) and axe (skips display:none elements). Added
an override so the input is visually hidden the same way
SelectableTile's is, with a focus-within outline on the row.

fix(multi-select): hide decorative option checkbox via CSS (#3430)

The earlier tabindex="-1" fix (113ed03cd) correctly got the attribute
onto the <input>, but axe-core's nested-interactive check doesn't
treat a negative tabindex (or aria-hidden) as sufficient to exclude an
element from "focusable descendant" -- confirmed by reading the rule's
own source (usesUnreliableHidingStrategy checks tabIndex < 0
specifically to flag this exact case) and empirically (adding
aria-hidden="true" alongside tabindex="-1" did not clear the
violation). Only genuine CSS hiding (display/visibility/
content-visibility) satisfies it.

Add a decorative prop to Checkbox that hides the <input> via
display: none when set, kept independent of tabindex so passing
tabindex="-1" for unrelated reasons doesn't silently also hide the
checkbox. :checked sibling-selector styling continues to work on a
display:none input, so the visual checkmark is unaffected. MultiSelect
passes the new prop for its option checkboxes, whose checked-state
authority is already the option's own aria-checked.

refactor(context-menu): remove dead safe-triangle hover check (#3625)

ContextMenuOption positions its submenu at the parent option's own
right edge (rootMenuPosition[0] + the <li>'s width), which always
equals the right edge of the containing <ul> since Carbon's
.bx--menu-option has no explicit width and .bx--menu has no
horizontal padding. The anchor and floating edges isInSafeTriangle
receives are therefore always identical, making its containment
check's denominator exactly 0 and every comparison NaN, i.e. always
false - the same degenerate case found while porting this behavior
to MenuItem.

The check was dead weight rather than a bug: the submenu <ul> is a
DOM descendant of the parent <li> (not portaled), so moving the
pointer onto it never fires mouseleave on the parent to begin with,
and mouseenter already cancels the close timer on re-entry. Drop the
triangle math, the mousePosition tracking, and the window mousemove
listener it required, and cover the flush-adjacent hover transfer
with a regression test.

perf(tabs): batch tab/content registration into a single store flush

synchronously during mount, each re-deriving tabsById/contentById (keyBy)
and re-triggering every already-mounted Tab's store subscriptions — O(n^2)

N synchronous registrations into a single microtask-deferred flush.

100 tabs 1.72s -> 20.33ms (~85x).

Caught a real bug along the way: afterUpdate fires once for free right
after initial mount, before the batched flush lands, so eagerly setting
needsDomSync inside add()/remove() let that empty-data afterUpdate consume
the flag before the real correction could run, silently breaking
selectedId-based initial selection. Fixed by setting needsDomSync inside
the batched update itself so it lands in the same cycle as the real data.

the signal this was a logic bug and not just test timing.

perf(overflow-menu): batch item registration into a single store flush

perf(user-avatar-group): batch avatar registration into a single store flush

during onMount, each re-sorting the whole registry by DOM position
(compareDocumentPosition) and re-triggering an O(n) DOM style pass via the
stackOrder reactive block plus every already-mounted avatar's own store
subscription — O(n^2 log n) for N avatars mounting at once. Reuses
src/utils/batchStoreUpdates.js (added for the Tabs fix, reused for

queue, not just register(), so a direct update never sees a stale array

had prior cross-Svelte-version ordering bugs with a deferred (afterUpdate)
approach. Confirmed that concern doesn't apply to a plain microtask:
sortByDomOrder reads live DOM position via compareDocumentPosition, so its
result doesn't depend on when it runs, only on final DOM layout -- and a
microtask doesn't touch Svelte's scheduler the way afterUpdate does. All 11
existing tests (DOM-reorder and stackOrder="first" index assertions
included) pass unchanged in outcome, needing only await tick() added.

snapping back. Also normalize directly in the Tab handler rather
than relying solely on afterUpdate, since Tab moves focus
asynchronously and afterUpdate can still see the input as focused
when it runs.

never touched the DOM in a way consumers could observe: bind:value
sets the property directly, so the native "input" event that
typing produces (and this component forwards) never fired.

button observable the same way typing is.

fix(list-box): use singular clear label for exactly one selection

items" instead of "Clear selected item".

that this component's reactive value binding and tabindex-less

fix(menu): prevent mouse focus on disabled MenuItem

A tabindex="-1" element still receives focus by default on click,
and handleClick returns early for disabled items without moving
focus elsewhere, so a click could leave DOM focus stuck on a
disabled row. Guards with preventDefault on mousedown.

Also adds regression coverage for submenu viewport flipping,
submenu-close/parent-menu independence, and open-menu focus
stability, confirming those already work correctly here: this
port's submenus share the same FloatingPortal positioning pipeline
as top-level menus (unlike React's separate per-submenu floating

re-running on every render.

supplementary description, not error association. aria-errormessage

as a direct child of HeaderPanelLinks' <ul>, which only <li> elements

fix(toggle-tip): resolve outside-click through shadow DOM boundaries

A click inside a shadow root retargets event.target to the shadow
host for listeners outside it, so isOutsideClick incorrectly saw a
click inside a shadow-DOM descendant as outside. composedPath()
carries the true path and is now consulted too. Shared by every
dismiss-on-outside-click consumer (Toggletip, Popover, ComboBox,
Dropdown, MultiSelect, OverflowMenu, Menu, ContextMenu, SearchMenu,
UIShell).

fix(clickable-tile): fire click handler on Space, not just Enter

Space never fires a native click on a link, so the consumer's
on:click handler only ran on Enter (via the native <a href> click),
while Space merely toggled the tile's own clicked state. Dispatch a
real click for Space (and for Enter without href, which also has no
native click) so both keys behave the same as a mouse click.

the max endpoint; floor-based delta causing fp drift). This port's

coverage instead of a behavior change.

Adds regression coverage confirming clicking a link menu item
collapses its parent HeaderNavMenu. Already worked correctly here:

catches bubbled clicks from any item regardless of type, unlike

already forwards attributes like maxlength to the input. Most of the
remaining batch-2 ComboBox commits (menu-highlight sync, active-item

or were already fixed by a prior pass (ad99a86's blur/toggle-close

close without a new selection. The upstream React bug was a downshift

selectedItem); this component's selectedId is only ever written by
the explicit selection handlers, so the bug class doesn't exist here.

Typed or pasted localized digits were silently dropped instead of parsed.

form autofill heuristics). Suppress webkit's own decoration/cancel
button in favor of Carbon's, and drop the now-redundant role="searchbox"
since type="search" already implies it.

fix(search-menu): prevent native Escape-clear from reopening the menu

whose value change fires an input event that reset the dismissed flag and
reopened the menu. Preventing the default keydown action keeps the
existing close-without-clearing behavior intact.

Expanded child rows used a flat 3.5rem inset that didn't account for
selection columns, so content landed left of the parent row's own text
when selectable/radio was enabled.

Clicking select-all (or its checked/indeterminate display) considered
every item in the list, not just the ones visible under an active

see. Scopes both the toggle and the checked/indeterminate calculation

already closes correctly when focus moves outside; drop the redundant,
overly-broad window blur listener.

considered the href visited. Add plain-class rules alongside the

fix(menu): indent every item's label when any sibling is selectable/radio

Carbon computes indentation menu-wide: if any item in a menu is
selectable or radio, every sibling's label gets the extra gap so the
whole column stays aligned, not just the selectable/radio rows. The
previous per-item isIndented check left plain siblings (icon or
text-only) flush left, visibly out of line with checkbox/radio items
in the same menu, as shown by the new MenuItemIndentAlignment example
and the existing MenuItemRadioGroup example (its "Reset" action next
to a radio group).

item" flag via context, and MenuItem reads it for both whether to
reserve the leading icon box and whether to apply the indent class.

fix(menu): give the checkmark its own column, separate from the icon

Carbon's real menu-option markup puts a selectable/radio item's
checkmark in its own leading column, ahead of any custom icon, rather
than replacing the icon. The previous single-box approach dropped a
selectable/radio item's `icon` prop entirely and swapped in the
checkmark instead, so a menu mixing icon items with a checkbox group
(e.g. "Cut" next to "Bold" with its own icon) couldn't show both the
icon and the checkmark on the same row.

Menu now tracks two independent menu-wide column flags via context:
one for whether any item is selectable/radio (reserves the checkmark
column for every item), and one for whether any item sets `icon`
(reserves the icon column for every item). MenuItem renders both
columns based on the shared flags, with its own state (selected,
icon) filling each independently. The vendored `--indented` label
margin is no longer applied, since the columns' own widths now do
that spacing.

fix(search): prevent disabled expandable search from expanding (#3775)

The magnifier icon's click handler and the input's focus handler
set `expanded = true` without checking `disabled`, so a disabled
expandable Search still visually expanded. Mirrors upstream
carbon-react/web-components fix (PR #23172).

fix(data-table): guard toolbar hover styles with any-hover (#3776)

Wraps the search-container, magnifier-icon, and toolbar-action
:hover rules in `_data-table-action.scss` so they only apply on
hover-capable pointers. Complements the earlier row-hover fix in
`_data-table-core.scss`, which covers a separate file and left
these toolbar rules unguarded, causing stuck hover states after
a tap on touchscreens.

fix(data-table): keep expand column width stable with custom header widths

table-layout: fixed enforces the expand column's declared 32px
width exactly. Auto layout treats that width as a floor and grows
the column to fit the expand button's padding and icon, so it
normally renders at 40px. Setting a width/minWidth on any header
switches the table to fixed layout, so the expand chevron visibly
shrinks.

Add a fixedLayout prop to Table that applies a
bx--data-table--fixed-layout class, and pin the expand column back
to 40px for that class in SCSS.

Fixes #3777

fix(dropdown): reserve field padding for the clear button

The field only padded for the menu chevron, so a long selected

docs(dropdown): add truncated item to clearable example

fix(list-box): stop stale DOM read from stranding the highlight class

register() checked a node's --active class straight off the DOM to
decide whether to keep it highlighted, but that class is patched on by
ListBoxMenuItem's own class: directive later in the same update cycle.
Deselecting an item (e.g. MultiSelect's clear button) tripped the race:
the stale read saw --active still present and kept --highlighted stuck
on the row forever. The cursor now tracks active ids itself instead of
reading the DOM back.

feat(dropdown): add openOnClear and a programmatic clear() method

Matches ComboBox: clearing used to always close the menu with no way
to refocus or reopen it. clear() now focuses the field by default
(disable with { focus: false }) and reopens the menu when passed
{ open: true }; openOnClear applies that automatically to the clear
button and the Delete/Backspace shortcut.

feat(multi-select): add openOnClear and a programmatic clear() method

Same parity gap as Dropdown/ComboBox: clearing left focus wherever the
click landed and never reopened the menu. clear() now focuses the
field (inputRef when filterable, fieldRef otherwise) by default,
disable with { focus: false }, and reopens the menu when passed
{ open: true }; openOnClear applies that automatically to the clear
button and the Delete/Backspace shortcut.
